claims: A mortgage is a type of loan used to purchase or refinance a home or other real estate.
The property itself serves as collateral to secure the debt in a mortgage.
The borrower agrees to make regular payments consisting of principal and interest.
If the borrower fails to make payments, the lender may take ownership of the property through a process called foreclosure.
Lenders evaluate credit score, income, debt-to-income (DTI) ratio, and property type to determine mortgage eligibility.
The interest rate of a fixed-rate mortgage stays the same for the entire life of the loan.
The interest rate of an adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) is fixed for an initial period and then adjusts periodically based on market indexes such as the SOFR.
Conventional loans are not insured by the federal government.
FHA loans are designed for low-to-moderate-income borrowers.
FHA loans require down payments as low as 3.5%.
VA loans are available to veterans and service members.
VA loans have 0% down payment options.
USDA loans are targeted at rural homebuyers with low-to-moderate income.
As of March 30, 2026, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was over 6.5%.
On March 26, 2026, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.38%.
On March 26, 2026, the 15-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 5.75%.
APR (Annual Percentage Rate) represents the true yearly cost of the loan, including interest, fees, and points.
1 point equals 1% of the loan amount.
Points are prepaid interest that can be paid upfront to lower the interest rate.
An assumable mortgage is a feature where a buyer can take over the seller's existing lower-rate mortgage rather than obtaining a new one.
